==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|ingage}} {{qualifier|obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*wedʰ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|engagen}}, from {{der|en|fro|engagier|t=to pledge, engage}}, from {{der|en|fro|en-|t=in, under}} + {{m|fro|gage|t=pledge}}, from {{der|en|frk|*wadi|t=pledge}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wadją|t=pledge, guarantee}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wedʰ-|t=to pledge, redeem a pledge; guarantee, bail}}, equivalent to {{af|en|en-|gage}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|weddian|t=to engage, covenant, undertake}}, {{cog|de|wetten|t=to bet, wager}}, {{cog|is|veðja|t=to wager}}. More at {{l|en|wed}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪnˈɡeɪd͡ʒ/|/ɛnˈɡeɪd͡ʒ/}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-engage.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪdʒ|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L6932}}
{{en-verb}}

# ''To interact socially.''
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[engross]] or [[hold]] the [[attention]] of; to keep busy or occupied.
##: {{syn|en|immerse}}
##* {{RQ:Pope Works 1751|volume=I|title=Messiah|lines=55–56|page=40|passage=Thus ſhall mankind his guardian care '''engage''', / The promis'd father of the future age.}}
## {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To draw into [[conversation]].
##* {{RQ:Hawthorne Scarlet Letter|Introductory|passage=the difficult task of '''engaging''' him in conversation}}
## To [[attract]], to [[please]]; {{lb|en|archaic}} to [[fascinate]] or [[win over]] (someone).
##* {{RQ:Spectator|issue=106|date=2 July 1711|page=74|passage=This humanity and good nature '''engages''' every body to him, so that when he is pleasant upon any of them all his family are in a good humour, and none so much as the person whom he diverts himself with: {{...}}}}
# ''To interact antagonistically.''
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[enter]] into [[conflict]] with (an [[enemy]]).
##* '''1698-1699''', {{w|Edmund Ludlow}}, ''Memoirs''
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To enter into [[battle]].
# ''To interact contractually.''
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[arrange]] to [[employ]] or [[use]] (a worker, a space, etc.).
##* {{RQ:Orczy Miss Elliott|chapter=The Affair at the Novelty Theatre|passage=For this scene, a large number of supers are '''engaged''', and in order to further swell the crowd, practically all the available stage hands have to ‘walk on’ dressed in various coloured dominoes, and all wearing masks.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[guarantee]] or [[promise]] (to do something).
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[bind]] through legal or moral obligation (to do something, ''especially'' to [[marry]]) {{qualifier|usually in passive}}.
##: {{ux|en|They were '''engaged''' last month! They're planning to have the wedding next year.}}
##* {{RQ:d'Urfey Old Mode|page=1|passage={{...}} Love is a ſort of Devotion too, and not only ſhould beget Reſpect, but likevviſe '''ingage''' Patience.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To [[pledge]], [[pawn]] (one's property); to put (something) at risk or on the line; to [[mortgage]] (houses, land).
##* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=II|canto=VII|passage=Thou that doest liue in later times, must wage / Thy workes for wealth, and life for gold '''engage'''.}}
# ''To interact mechanically.''
## To [[mesh]] or [[interlock]] (of machinery, especially a [[clutch]]).
##: {{ux|en|Whenever I '''engage''' the clutch, the car stalls out.}}
## {{lb|en|engineering|transitive}} To come into gear with.
##: The teeth of one cogwheel '''engage''' those of another.
## {{lb|en|intransitive|or|transitive}} To activate a [[lock]].
##: {{ux|en|He '''engaged''' the lock on the door.}}
##: {{ux|en|The lock '''engaged''' automatically when the door was shut.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[entangle]].

====Antonyms====
* {{antsense|to cause to mesh or interlock}} {{l|en|disengage}}
